note: Adapted from the species description of Aderitotermes fossor in Sands (1972), originally in English: the species lacks soldiers and only the alate and the worker are described; measurement-table headers, figure numbers, locality and biological records are not translated, and figures damaged by OCR in the measurement tables are omitted; mandibular and cephalic pilosity characters covered by the generic diagnosis are not repeated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: This species is selected as the type species of Aderitotermes: although clearly distinct from the other genera, it is the most primitive member of the genus in having shorter apical teeth of the mandibles and an enteric valve armed with spines only. In this respect it resembles Amicotermes markedly, and Acholotermes also has a dense fringe of minute spines; the latter two genera have longer apical teeth but a similar enteric valve seating; in A. epius this seating tends to become dorsal, accompanied by elongation of the midgut-hindgut overlap.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish white, pilosity pale yellow, very sparse. Postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.25–0.27, Pcl/Ri 2.22–2.35. Apical teeth of the mandibles short, La/Li 0.60–0.64, Ra/Ri 0.78–0.88. Fore tibia slightly inflated, T1/Tw 4.21–4.62. The enteric valve seating is connected to the second hindgut pouch by a very long neck; all the enteric valve cushions are retracted and uniformly developed, bearing numerous long, distinct but fine spines posteriorly, the remainder smooth and without spines; the membranous wall of the valve bears long spines likewise between and outside the cushions, forming a complete fringe around the valve opening.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark brown, or reddish towards chestnut brown, darker above the ocelli, the dark area sometimes extending as striae towards the fontanelle; fontanelle circular, flat, about half the size of the ocellus, yellowish white, very distinct; median spot elliptical, flat, smaller than the fontanelle, concolorous with the head capsule; postclypeus brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal marking a weakly developed flat crescent, concolorous with the head capsule or slightly paler; antennae pale yellowish brown. Pronotum dark brown, meso- and metanotum brown; femora pale yellowish brown, tibiae and tarsi paler. Abdominal tergites brown, dorsolateral spiracles dark brown, sternites pale brown with the middle yellow, ventrolateral spiracles brown; cerci yellow. Posterior margin of the head capsule evenly rounded; ocelli of medium size, separated from the compound eye by half or more of their own least diameter; postclypeus weakly to moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.24–0.30, Pcl/Ra 2.37–3.00, posterior margin evenly rounded, median suture distinct. Composite ratio of mandibular and notal measurements L1/M.N 1.50–2.05.
